title: Lab-in-the-Loop at Compute Speed — Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
subtitle: How Leash Bio tamed DELs, the assay that traumatizes everyone, and used the data to catch cheating models. And why that same data is perfect for AI agents learning to think like chemists.
intro: A few years ago I stumbled upon Leash Bio’s Substack , and was hooked. Be it their Kaggle competition that showed that no, we really haven’t solved protein-ligand binding , or their crazy discovery that knowing a molecule’s author is perhaps all you need to know to predict how good it is . Their substack — or at least Owl Posting ’s 1 deep dive on them — should be required reading for any scientist trying to do chemistry with AI.

So I was super excited to finally be able to sit down with Ian Quigley from Leash Bio, and pick his brain. Leash specializes in DNA Encoded Libraries (aka “DELs”), a way of collecting ridiculously high-throughput interaction data between proteins and small molecules. 2 Before I discovered Leash, I had heard nothing but horror stories from DEL users. And yet, Ian and friends somehow found a way to tame the beast, extracting clean and reproducible data that is just perfect for large scale modeling. Without teasing too much, the answer comes down to epistemic rigor, and an incredible conviction that you just have to Do The Thing.

It gets even better! Near the end of this episode, Ian teases something his team was just playing with when we recorded: an AI playground for agents to do verifiable scientific reasoning. They discovered the data they had spent the last few years collecting could provide tens of thousands of “lab-in-the-loop” simulations, just what an agent needs for scientific RL. Two months later, it’s matured into Minos, and today they’re releasing a full preprint , blog , and open dataset . We’ll be releasing a lightning podcast in a few days with an update. Stay tuned!
We had a blast with Ian, probably one of our most fun episodes to date. For both complete chemistry novices and expert AI x Bio practitioners, we think you’ll get something out of this.
The hands-down best bio blogger on the internet.
As always, the secret here is to map your problem to a combinatorial library and a readout using Next Generation Sequencing. We talk about this in depth in the podcast!

summary.one_liner: Leash Bio 馴服 DELs 數據抓出作弊模型，並將實驗資料轉為供 AI Agent 進行科學強化學習的模擬環境。

topics.title: 揭穿蛋白質結合預測的捷徑
topics.body: Leash Bio 透過 Kaggle 競賽揭露，業界尚未真正解決蛋白質與小分子配體結合的預測難題。他們更發現驚人事實：模型有時僅需得知分子的作者是誰，就能預測其表現，暴露出模型走捷徑的作弊現象。這突顯了對該領域預測模型進行嚴謹驗證的必要性。

topics.title: 馴服高難度 DELs 技術
topics.body: DNA Encoded Libraries (DELs) 能夠收集超高通量的蛋白質與小分子交互作用數據，但過去常因雜訊與再現性差而被視為使用者的夢魘。Leash Bio 透過嚴謹的認知態度與徹底執行的決心，克服了技術障礙。他們成功提煉出乾淨且高重現性的數據，為大規模 AI 建模奠定基礎。

topics.title: 組合庫與次世代定序的核心解法
topics.body: 在生物化學數據採集的技術架構上，核心秘密在於問題抽象與轉譯。Leash Bio 的做法是將目標問題映射至組合庫（combinatorial library），並搭配 Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) 作為高通量讀出手段。這種方法讓大規模數據採集能與計算速度接軌。

topics.title: Minos：AI Agent 的科學推理模擬場
topics.body: Leash Bio 將過去幾年累積的實驗數據，轉化為數萬次 Lab-in-the-Loop 的模擬環境。這為 AI Agent 進行科學推理的強化學習（RL）提供了絕佳的驗證場域。這項成果進一步成熟為 Minos 專案，並公開了預印本論文、部落格與開源資料集。

insights.title: 以可驗證的環境支援 Agent 科學強化學習
insights.body: 訓練具備專業領域推理能力的 Agent 時，單靠靜態文字生成難以確認正確性。將高通量真實實驗數據封裝為高擬真的模擬環境，能提供 Agent 進行 RL 訓練所需的即時驗證回饋。

insights.title: 嚴防評測指標中的特徵洩漏與作弊捷徑
insights.body: 在設計 AI 評測工作流時，需嚴密審查非因果關係的中繼資料（如作者、來源標籤等）。若未妥善隔離這些線索，模型容易學會走捷徑產生虛假的高準確率。

insights.title: 源頭數據的嚴謹性決定 AI 流程上限
insights.body: 面對大規模但雜訊極高的資料流，工程師必須在管線源頭落實高度的認知嚴謹度（epistemic rigor）。只有提煉出乾淨且可重現的基準資料，後續的建模與 Agent 推理才有實用價值。

guests.name: Ian Quigley
guests.intro: 任職於 Leash Bio，專注於馴服高通量 DELs 數據並打造供 AI Agent 進行科學推理強化學習的模擬環境。

summary.one_liner: Leash Bio tames DELs data to catch cheating models, turning experimental data into a simulation environment for scientific reinforcement learning with AI Agents.

topics.title: Debunking shortcuts in protein-binding prediction
topics.body: Through a Kaggle competition, Leash Bio revealed that the industry has not truly solved the challenge of predicting protein-small molecule ligand binding. Even more strikingly, they discovered that models could sometimes predict performance simply by knowing the molecule's author, exposing shortcut learning behaviors. This underscores the necessity of rigorous validation for predictive models in this domain.

topics.title: Taming challenging DELs technology
topics.body: DNA Encoded Libraries (DELs) can collect ultra-high-throughput protein-small molecule interaction data, but they were historically seen as a practitioner's nightmare due to noise and poor reproducibility. Through epistemic rigor and disciplined execution, Leash Bio overcame these technical hurdles. They successfully distilled clean, highly reproducible data, laying the groundwork for large-scale AI modeling.

topics.title: The core solution: Combinatorial libraries and Next-Generation Sequencing
topics.body: In the technical architecture of biochemical data acquisition, the key lies in problem abstraction and translation. Leash Bio's approach maps the target problem onto a combinatorial library and pairs it with Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) as a high-throughput readout method. This strategy allows large-scale data acquisition to keep pace with computational speed.

topics.title: Minos: A scientific reasoning simulation arena for AI Agents
topics.body: Leash Bio transformed years of accumulated experimental data into tens of thousands of Lab-in-the-Loop simulation environments. This provides an ideal proving ground for AI Agents performing reinforcement learning (RL) on scientific reasoning. This effort culminated in Project Minos, alongside a published preprint, blog post, and open-source datasets.

insights.title: Supporting Agent scientific reinforcement learning with verifiable environments
insights.body: When training Agents with domain-specific reasoning capabilities, relying solely on static text generation makes correctness hard to verify. Encapsulating high-throughput real-world experimental data into high-fidelity simulation environments provides the immediate validation feedback required for Agent RL training.

insights.title: Guarding against feature leakage and shortcut learning in evaluation metrics
insights.body: When designing AI evaluation workflows, non-causal metadata (e.g., authors, source tags) must be rigorously audited. If these signals are not properly isolated, models readily learn shortcuts that yield spuriously high accuracy.

insights.title: Upstream data rigor dictates the upper bound of AI pipelines
insights.body: Faced with massive, highly noisy data streams, engineers must enforce strong epistemic rigor at the source of the pipeline. Downstream modeling and Agent reasoning only provide practical value if clean, reproducible ground-truth data is distilled first.

guests.name: Ian Quigley
guests.intro: Working at Leash Bio, focused on taming high-throughput DELs data and building simulation environments for scientific reasoning reinforcement learning in AI Agents.
